segments.text: International Law explains the legal rules governing relations among states, international organizations and, increasingly, individuals. FPSC’s outline moves from sources and statehood to treaties, disputes, force, responsibility, jurisdiction and armed conflict.

items.text: Learn Article 38 of the ICJ Statute early; it organizes the sources topic.
Use treaties and ICJ cases as examples, but only where accurately remembered.
Distinguish jus ad bellum (use of force) from international humanitarian law (conduct during conflict).
Use short issue-rule-application-conclusion structure for problem questions.

segments.text: Start with sources and legal personality, then move to treaties, dispute settlement and state powers. Keep the use-of-force rules separate from humanitarian law. Finish by linking responsibility, jurisdiction, diplomacy, conflict and neutrality to the same basic idea: states possess rights but exercise them within international obligations.
